clue.text: Cheesy type of European porno might one say?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a blue-veined cheese from Denmark
second meaning: a blue film is a pornographic one, and this one comes from a Scandinavian country

explanation.surface: A smutty question about whether a cheesy European porn film has a name.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'blue' film is slang for a pornographic one, so a film from Denmark would share its name with the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish Blue is a well-known soft, blue-veined cheese, and blue film is a common term for pornography.

clue.text: Work out and go around without a top

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, so losing it removes the opening letter

parts.note: to go around is to turn in a circle

explanation.surface: Someone exercising, then jogging round a track while shirtless.
explanation.walkthrough: REVOLVE loses its first letter R to leave EVOLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to develop gradually, as a plan or idea unfolds and takes shape over time.

clue.text: Pretty gutted act will restrict Penthouse?

indicators.note: restricting something means holding it in, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a deed is an act
a penthouse is a top-floor flat

explanation.surface: Disappointment that a law will curb the men's magazine Penthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P suggests the magazine, but it is just a top-floor apartment. 'Gutted' is British slang for bitterly disappointed.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling deflated means being dispirited and let down, which British slang calls gutted.

clue.text: Unwilling to drop liberal swear word

indicators.note: dropping something leaves it out, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: loath means reluctant
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to give up a liberal habit of cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: LOATH without L leaves OATH.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a profanity or curse, as well as a solemn promise; here it is the rude kind.

clue.text: Needing nosh, celeb visits every dive at front

parts.note: a celebrity is a star

indicators.note: the letter at the front of each word is the one that is taken

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A hungry celebrity slumming it in every seedy bar to find food.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is British slang for food, and starved means badly in need of something to eat.

clue.text: Ingredient in delicious US highly-spiced dish

indicators.note: an ingredient is part of a mixture, so the answer is one part of the run of words

parts.note: found across the end of the first word, the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Something that goes into a tasty, hot American meal.
explanation.walkthrough: deliciouS US HIghly gives SUSHI; the spicy surface suits a curry, not raw fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese preparation of vinegared rice with raw fish, served as a course or meal.

clue.text: Bedding rampant goer consumes very excited leader

indicators.note: rampant means rearing up on hind legs, so in a down entry the word rises and is read bottom to top
consuming something takes it inside, so one piece swallows the others

parts.note: a stud is a sexually active man, a goer
V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, the one at the head

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A lusty lover in bed overwhelming a thrilled boss.
explanation.walkthrough: STUD reversed is DUTS, which takes in V and E: DU(VE)TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Duvets are quilts filled with feathers or synthetic fibre, used as the covering on a bed.

clue.text: Delight old flame and harlots regularly

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Pleasing a former lover and some prostitutes on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to fill them with joy or elation, a dated sense close to thrill.

clue.text: Pound Tom owes for no-frills sexual liaison?

indicators.note: to pound something is to batter it, so the letters are beaten into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tom owing a pound for a basic paid encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the money Tom owes; it is the signal to rearrange. The question mark admits the definition is playful: two people, nothing fancy like a threesome.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a pair of people, and a plain encounter between just two people lacks any extra participants.

clue.text: Way to open excellent sparkling wine

indicators.note: to open something is to get inside it, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as I
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: How best to uncork a bottle of good fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is the standard crossword 'excellent', with the digit 1 standing in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sweet Italian fizzy white wine from Piedmont, often called Asti Spumante.

clue.text: High-spirited thug in hearing for job?

indicators.note: something in hearing is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: lively means high-spirited and a hood is a thug, short for hoodlum

explanation.surface: An exuberant hooligan turning up at an interview for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lively hood' said out loud matches the answer; only the first part changes spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A livelihood is the means by which someone earns a living, such as an occupation.

clue.text: This side playing can be most attractive

indicators.note: playing about with something moves it around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports team being told it looks its best when it is on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy is British slang for good-looking, so the superlative means the most handsome or sexy.

clue.text: Permanent marker?

parts.note: surface reading: a felt pen whose ink will not wash off
setter's reading: something that marks the skin for good

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a stationery item, a Sharpie, but read literally it is anything leaving a lasting mark, here inked into the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a design made with ink under the skin, which cannot be removed easily.

clue.text: Flapper mixed up in ribald riot

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled, so the letters are thrown into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A 1920s good-time girl caught up in a bawdy brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flapper' suggests a jazz-age young woman, but it is anything that flaps its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: The tailorbird is an Asian songbird that stitches leaves together for its nest, and birds flap their wings.

clue.text: Observe activity of parasitic insects on river

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so the insects go second

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
lice are parasites living on hair or feathers

explanation.surface: A nature study watching bugs that feed off hosts by a riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' puts A after B, so the insects follow the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To police a place or process is to monitor and regulate what goes on there.

clue.text: A Parisian bloke sat on by priest and tart?

indicators.note: in a down entry, being sat on by something puts that thing on top, so the clergyman comes first

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for priest
un is French for a
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A Frenchman being sat on by a clergyman and a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat on by' in a down clue puts the priest on top of the rest. 'Tart' suggests a woman of easy virtue; it is the adjective for sharp-tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent means having a sharply strong taste or smell, close to tart or sour.

clue.text: Bum had scrap in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: bum is slang for poor or faulty, so the letters are in a bad order and must be fixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tramp got into a fight at a homeless shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' reads as a tramp, the subject of the sentence; it is the adjective meaning poor, signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash pad is a place to sleep for a night or two, usually a friend's sofa or spare room.

clue.text: Warning: immoral acts will follow a bit of deviancy

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter
vice is wicked behaviour

explanation.surface: A caution that dabbling in perversion leads to depravity.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is guidance, and a warning is advice about what to avoid.

clue.text: When record cut by edgy members of Love is out?

indicators.note: being cut by something means it is pushed in between, splitting the pieces

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the members at the edges of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A question about when a record by a nervy band is being released.
explanation.walkthrough: Love was a 1960s American band, which feeds the music picture; 'is out' sounds like a release date, but out here means unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone asleep is out cold, unconscious in slumber, so being out is the idiom here.

clue.text: Woman with no time for smack knocked back beer

indicators.note: having no time means the abbreviation for time is taken out of the word

parts.note: a smack is a taste or flavour, a tang
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: knocked back suggests going backwards, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A woman who, too busy for heroin, downed a beer instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' wants to be heroin or a slap; here it is a flavour, as in 'a smack of garlic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela is a female given name, and crosswords often define first names simply as woman or girl.

clue.text: Presumed deviant ups dope around start of summer

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap the extra one
deviant means straying from the norm, so the letters stray out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone assumed a pervert would increase their drug intake at the start of the warm season.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposed means assumed to be true without proof, so it matches presumed as a past participle.

clue.text: Go-Go's singer

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for urinating
another word for the same bodily function

explanation.surface: Naming the lead vocalist of the Go-Go's, the American girl band.
explanation.walkthrough: The Go-Go's were a 1980s US pop band; the hyphenated name splits into two words for relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewee is a songbird, either the lapwing in Britain or the Australian magpie-lark, so it is a bird that sings.

clue.text: Hoskins is one for drugs and sex, judge admitted

indicators.note: being admitted means let inside, so one letter goes within the others

parts.note: E is ecstasy, and two make the plural
J is the abbreviation for judge
it is slang for sex

explanation.surface: The setter confessing to a fondness for drugs and sex in front of a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoskins is the setter, mocking himself. EE and IT take in J: EE(J)IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eejit is Irish and Scottish slang for an idiot, and the setter jokingly calls himself a fool.

clue.text: Heated Celt beat competitive sort in many events

indicators.note: beat as a past participle means battered, so the letters are knocked into shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hot-headed Irish or Scottish competitor winning across a range of contests.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlete is an athlete who competes in the ten track and field disciplines of the decathlon.

clue.text: Egyptian dancing girl seen in Rueil-Malmaison

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it, so the answer lies within the name

parts.note: found in the middle of the place name

explanation.surface: A belly dancer spotted in a town west of Paris, home of Josephine's château.
explanation.walkthrough: Rueil-Malmaison is a suburb of Paris; the answer sits in rueil-mALMAison.
explanation.definitionFit: An alma, or almah, is a professional female singer and dancer in Egypt, a crossword-only word.

clue.text: After inhaling joint, heckle disgraced former Tory leader

indicators.note: inhaling takes something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to heckle is to jeer or boo
J is slang for a cannabis joint

explanation.surface: Jeering at a scandal-hit ex-prime minister after he has had a smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: BOO takes in J: BO(J)O. BoJo is the tabloid nickname for Boris Johnson, the British prime minister who resigned in 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson led the Conservative Party and left office amid scandal, and the press calls him BoJo.

clue.text: Vagabond polishing off last of beer and a port

indicators.note: polishing off means finishing and getting rid of, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a tramp is a vagabond

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tramp downing the dregs of his beer and a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAMP without R is TAMP. 'Port' looks like the fortified wine in this drinking scene, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a city in Florida on Tampa Bay with a major seaport.

clue.text: In short, Frenchman's out-of-head drunk clown!

indicators.note: something short has been cut off, so the last letter is dropped
with its head gone, a word loses its first letter

parts.note: Pierre is a typical French man's name
a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A Frenchman, out of his mind with drink, is a buffoon.
explanation.walkthrough: PIERRE cut short is PIERR, and SOT beheaded is OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the sad pantomime figure in white face and loose costume from French and Italian comedy.
